where: the one build queue (/root/loop.sh on blaze-vm): the only compiler a lane has
what: A lane cannot compile before it pushes: the brief says to push to `int-1112` and build that, and a push that does not compile fails the build of all eight lanes until it is fixed. This lane's first commit had 34 compile errors (a wrongly placed hunk, row onsave-1112-1). It was pushed to a scratch branch (`onsave-1112`) and built with `loop.sh onsave-1112`, so nobody else saw it; each such build switches /root/blaze to another branch and back, and waited 5 to 15 minutes behind three or four other lanes' calls.
cost: each compile error costs a queue turn: 10 to 20 minutes a round, four rounds before the first green build
cause: one tree, one target directory and one lock for eight lanes; a check of blaze-cargo alone is part of that same build
whys: a cold build per lane was the cost the one VM removed (H12)
no lane has a place to run `cargo check` on its own diff
class: a shared branch that is also the only place code is first compiled
prevention: not built: a second, check-only tree on the VM (`cargo check -p <crate>` of a pushed scratch commit, its own target directory, outside the build lock) so a lane's compile errors cost one minute and no queue turn; until then, the how-to: push to a scratch branch first (lane_commit.py's `push`)
workaround: a scratch branch built through the same queue
